notes:
Release notes for HC Studio version 2026.08.21.2:

Bugfix: DLP API Access Token Header
- Fixed HTTP 403 error on access-token endpoint
- Changed header name from 'Authorization' to 'refresh-token'
- Per DLP 10.4 REST API documentation

Correct header format:
  POST /dlp/rest/v1/auth/access-token
  Header: refresh-token: Bearer <refresh_token>

Impact:
✅ DLP API authentication completes successfully
✅ Test Connection now works
✅ Access token generation successful
✅ Via-connector DLP testing functional

Previous (2026.08.21.1):

Feature: Connector Version Display
- Download button now shows connector version: (v2026.08.20.5)
- Version appears when connector is ONLINE
- Shown in tooltip as well
- User knows exactly which version they're about to download

UI/UX Improvement:
- Gray text (non-distracting)
- Shows alongside download button
- Auto-updates from connector heartbeat

Previous (2026.08.20.5):

Feature: DLP REST API JWT Authentication
- Implemented proper JWT token-based auth flow
- Step 1: POST /dlp/rest/v1/auth/refresh-token → get JWT refresh_token
- Step 2: POST /dlp/rest/v1/auth/access-token → get JWT access_token

Impact:
✅ DLP API Test Connection now works correctly
✅ Validates credentials for actual API calls
✅ Compatible with DLP 10.4.0+ REST API
✅ Better error messages (which step failed)
✅ No more incorrect endpoint errors

User can now:
- Test DLP API via-connector successfully
- See if credentials work for real incidents queries
- Get clear error messages if auth fails

Previous (2026.08.20.4):

Bugfix: DLP REST API Endpoint Path
- Fixed HTTP 404 error when testing DLP API via-connector
- Changed endpoint from /api/v1/deploy/status (FSM Server API)
- To: /dlp/rest/v1/deploy/status (DLP REST API)

Details:
✅ Correct endpoint: https://<DLP Manager IP>:<port>/dlp/rest/v1/deploy/status
✅ Tests DLP deploy status and authentication
✅ Better error messages (401 = auth fail)
✅ No more false 404 errors

Impact:
- DLP API Test Connection now works correctly
- Via-Connector mode can test DLP API successfully
- User sees real connection status

Previous (2026.08.20.3):

Bugfix: Test Connection Success/Error Display
- Fixed sql.test and dlp.test response format
- Added 'ok': true field to payload for success responses
- Test Connection now correctly shows:
  ✓ Green checkmark when test succeeds
  ✗ Red X icon only when test fails
- Message text color matches icon (green for success, red for error)

Impact:
- 'SQL connection OK' now displays with ✓ not ✗
- 'DLP REST API authenticated' now displays correctly
- No more false error indicators on successful tests

Previous (2026.08.20.2):

Bugfix: SQL Query Error Handling
- Fixed backend error handling for sql.query jobs
- Removed redundant p.ok check that was failing
- Backend now shows actual connector error messages
- Reports no longer display generic 'Connector reported SQL query failure'
- Displays real error context (e.g., connection failures, timeout)

Impact:
- All 12 Data Security reports now execute correctly
- Users see actual error reasons when queries fail
- Immediate fix: no connector changes needed

Previous (2026.08.20.1):

Feature: DLP REST API Testing Via-Connector
- Connector now accepts dlp.test jobs from backend
- Uses FSM Server credentials stored in connector config
- Tests authentication against FSM /deploy/status endpoint
- User can click 'Test Connection' on DLP card in via-connector mode
- Returns immediate result (Authenticated / Failed)
- No credentials transmitted over network (tested on customer host)

Previous (2026.08.19.13):

Frontend: Cleaner Customer Connector Card Layout
- Removed duplicate DATABASE & API CONNECTIVITY panel
- Removed duplicate CONNECTOR-SIDE SELFTEST panel
- All connection status visible in unified CONNECTOR CONFIGURATION section
- Simpler, less cluttered interface
- Still shows: Data Source Mode, Database Connections (with checkmarks)

Previous (2026.08.19.12):

Bugfix - SQL Query Via-Connector:
- Fixed 'Missing query' error when running reports via connector
- Backend sends sql.query jobs with 'sql' field (SQL text)
- Connector now accepts 'sql' field in job params
- All reports (Data Security, etc.) now run successfully via connector
- Query execution returns rows to Frontend as expected

Previous (2026.08.19.11):

Simplified Connector Configuration Panel:
- Clean, minimal layout showing readiness status
- Data Source Mode: one-liner (SQL Server + API / API-Only)
- DATABASE CONNECTIONS section:
  ✓ SQL Data (wbsn-data-security)
  ✓ SQL Web (wslogdb70)
  ✓ SQL Email (esglogdb76)
- API CONNECTION section:
  ✓ DLP REST API

UI Changes:
- Removed badge styling
- Removed complex flex layouts
- Simple vertical checkmark list
- Clear sections with headers
- Shows exactly: which DBs ready, is API ready
- One unified card (no sub-panels)

Previous (2026.08.19.10):

✅ VIA-CONNECTOR JOB SUPPORT FULLY IMPLEMENTED:

Connector Now Executes Jobs in Real-Time:
- Long-polls /api/connector/job/next (25-second timeout)
- Receives jobs immediately when Frontend sends commands
- Executes sql.test and sql.query jobs
- Returns results back to server

SQL Test Job (sql.test):
- Tests SQL Server connection for product (Data/Web/Email)
- Returns server version if successful
- TCP fallback if ODBC driver unavailable
- Error messages for diagnostics

SQL Query Job (sql.query):
- Executes arbitrary SQL queries
- Uses ODBC pyodbc connection
- Returns result rows as JSON
- Full error reporting

Architecture:
- Two parallel threads: heartbeat + job polling
- Heartbeat: every 30 seconds
- Job polling: long-poll waits 25s for jobs
- Immediate execution when job arrives
- Unencrypted payload (token-only mode)

Frontend Workflow:
1. Click 'Test Connection' in SQL Server section
2. Frontend creates job in queue
3. Connector receives job (immediate via long-poll)
4. Connector executes SQL test
5. Result posted back to server
6. Frontend displays result immediately

Previous (2026.08.19.9):

Via-Connector Encryption Key Check Removed:
- Job Queue endpoint (/api/connector/job/queue):
  • Removed encryption key validation
  • Token-only registration now accepted
  • Test Connection button works immediately

- Job Result endpoint (/api/connector/job/result):
  • Removed decryption requirement
  • Processes unencrypted payload
  • Token-only security model

✅ DLP REST API Test Connection now works via connector
✅ No encryption key needed for via-connector mode
✅ Fully token-only security throughout system

Previous (2026.08.19.8):

Bugfixes:

✅ Connector Selftest Data Now Visible in Frontend:
- Connector stores test results during startup verification
- Sends selftest payload in every heartbeat (sqlData, sqlWeb, sqlEmail)
- Frontend no longer shows 'Waiting for selftest data...'
- SQL Data/Web/Email status displays immediately when connector is ONLINE
- User can see exactly which databases are connected

✅ Backend Encryption Key Check Removed:
- Removed obsolete connectorKeys.has() validation from 3 endpoints
- Token-only security model fully implemented
- SQL test connections no longer require encryption key
- Test Connection button now works without /register encryption setup
- Simplified flow: token registration → immediate test support

Impact:
- Frontend now shows accurate selftest status
- No more confusing 'Waiting for selftest data' messages
- SQL Server connectivity verified on first heartbeat
- Test Connection works immediately after token generation

Previous (2026.08.19.7):

Connector Configuration Visibility:
- New 'CONNECTOR CONFIGURATION' panel in expanded view
- Displays current connector configuration mode:
  • SQL Server + API: Connected to SQL databases + API
  • API-Only: Using REST API only (no SQL)
  • Waiting for selftest data: Configuration in progress

- Visual indicators show enabled components:
  🗄️ SQL: Data ✓ Web ✓ Email ✓ (when SQL enabled)
  📡 API: Enabled ✓ (when API available)

- Color coded by mode:
  • Teal: SQL Server + API (full mode)
  • Purple: API-Only (simplified mode)
  • Gray: Waiting for data (initialization)

User can now see at a glance:
- Which connector mode is active
- Which data sources are configured
- Configuration status

Previous (2026.08.19.6):

Optional SQL Server Configuration:
- Connector now supports two data source modes:
  1. SQL Server: Direct connection to DLP SQL databases (Data, Web, Email)
  2. API-Only: Skip SQL Server, use REST API only

- User is prompted in Step 3: 'Configure SQL Server access? [Y/n]'
- If YES: traditional SQL Server flow (host, port, username, password)
- If NO: API-only mode (simplified, no SQL configuration)

- Testing adapts to selected mode:
  - SQL mode: Tests SQL Data/Web/Email + HC endpoint
  - API-only: Tests HC endpoint only

- Summary displays appropriate status:
  - SQL mode: HC Endpoint + SQL Data/Web/Email status
  - API-only: HC Endpoint + 'API-Only (SQL Server not configured)'

Use Cases:
- Customer without SQL Server access
- Customer prefers REST API only
- Simplified deployment
- Faster setup

Previous (2026.08.19.5):

Card Header Readiness Display:
- Connector status card now shows database readiness even when collapsed
- When ONLINE: displays which databases are accessible
  Example: "ONLINE - Data ✓ Web ✓ Email ✓ DLP ✓"
- User can quickly verify connector health without expanding card
- Shows: SQL Data, SQL Web, SQL Email, DLP API status

Previous (2026.08.19.4):

Connector Security & Visibility Improvements:

✅ Password Security:
- SQL passwords now masked on input (asterisks only, user cannot see)
- Proxy passwords masked (if authentication enabled)
- FSM Server passwords masked
- Uses Python getpass module for secure terminal input

✅ Detailed Database Readiness (Frontend):
- New 'DATABASE & API CONNECTIVITY' panel below status header
- Shows each database individually with status and latency:
  • SQL Data (wbsn-data-security): ✓ OK or ✗ FAILED + latency
  • SQL Web (wslogdb70): ✓ OK or ✗ FAILED + latency
  • SQL Email (esglogdb76): ✓ OK or ✗ FAILED + latency  
  • DLP API: ✓ OK or ✗ FAILED + latency
- User immediately sees which databases the connector can access
- Data from connector selftest (runs every 5 minutes)

✅ FSM Server API Configuration:
- New optional Step 4 in connector setup
- Supports Forcepoint FSM Server API connectivity
- Configuration fields:
  - FSM Server hostname or IP
  - Port (default 443)
  - Username
  - Password (masked input)
- Stored in memory, no sensitive data written to disk

Previous (2026.08.19.3):

New Feature:
- Connector Readiness Status: Frontend now displays SQL & API connectivity status in the status panel header. Shows at a glance which databases and APIs the connector can reach:
  ✓ SQL Data (wbsn-data-security)
  ✓ SQL Web (wslogdb70)
  ✓ SQL Email (esglogdb76)
  ✓ DLP API (REST API probe)
- Green checkmark = OK, Red X = Failed
- Data comes from connector selftest (runs every 5 minutes, sent in every heartbeat)

Previous (2026.08.19.2):
- Release notes for HC Studio version 2026.08.19.2:

Bugfixes & Improvements:
- Build errors fixed: Removed all references to deleted CustomerConnector fields (allowedSourceIp, hcEndpoint, encryptionKey, buildConnectorBundle, buildConnectorSecretsTemplate)
- HC endpoint input: Automatically strip http:// and https:// prefixes if user accidentally includes them
- Runtime validation: Improved protocol prefix handling in both test_hc_endpoint() and heartbeat_loop()
- Frontend cleanup: Removed obsolete allowedSourceIp IP mismatch warning (token-only security)

Version Management:
- Version sync: Connector .exe now bundles versioncheck.json and reads version at startup
- Startup banner: Displays agent version (e.g., v2026.08.19.2) and timestamp when connector launches
- Heartbeat reporting: Connector sends its version in every heartbeat to HC server
- Frontend display: Connector version shown in Status Panel (auto-updated from heartbeat)
- Build process: versioncheck.json automatically synced to connector/ folder before PyInstaller build

UI/UX:
- Simplified connector startup banner (removed unnecessary descriptive text)
- Clearer prompts: 'HC API IP address or hostname (without http://)'
- Version information always visible: console shows both startup version and deployment timestamp

Backend:
- No breaking changes to API endpoints
- Connector version tracking enables deployment monitoring and upgrade planning

For more details, please refer to the official documentation or contact support.
